scope: Wardweave and Cinderweave gameplay approved and implemented October 7; mage armor v2 worn appearance approved October 8. The other four clothing packages remain proposals.

accepted: Robes use the chest armor slot, give very little armor, increase maximum mana, and have an additional effect.
Four wool blocks must all match. Their color determines the finished cloth color; mixed colors do not craft.
Cloth may be dyed later. Belts, fastenings, cuffs and patches keep their identifying colors.
Wardweave and Cinderweave each use eight offerings around an empty Spellstone.
Every magical armor piece has durability. Normal damaging hits cause armor wear; hits absorbed by the robe’s magic still wear that robe, including full prevention.
Do not charge extra durability simply for activating an effect or keeping it active. Charge each eligible hit once; protected damage cannot make the robe unbreakable.
Trait-driven duration and protection can grow without arbitrary power ceilings. Actual damage prevented cannot exceed the hit; persistent pocket counts remain separate design decisions.
Ordinary compatible armor enchantments are allowed, but Unbreaking and Mending are excluded to preserve the authored durability and magical-material repair rules.
Each robe: 2 armor points, zero toughness, +25 maximum mana. A robe takes the normal pool from 100 to 125.
Equipping extra capacity does not refill mana. Taking it off clamps mana to the smaller pool; recovery speed stays the same.
Ability recovery belongs to the wearer. Swapping, repairing or dyeing another copy does not reset it.
Wardweave and Cinderweave begin with 80 durability. One corresponding magical thread repairs 20 durability at an anvil; dyeing and repair preserve components.
proposed: The hood and each pair of boots: 1 armor point and zero toughness. Dawnsight could also give +10 maximum mana.
finishingProposal: The remaining hood/boots packages could start with 55/65 durability; these are still proposals.
Corresponding-thread repair is implemented for both approved robes; repair materials and quantities for the remaining clothing still need review.
Dyeing and repairs preserve stored objects, enchantments and item identity.

items.name: Wardweave Robes
behavior: A hit that actually deals health damage creates a four-second ward. That triggering hit keeps its normal damage; canceled or fully blocked hits do not arm it.
The next eligible hit spends the single charge and loses up to 2 HP (one heart) before ordinary armor and other protections. A smaller hit still spends the whole charge.
Time multiplies duration; Force and Amplify multiply protection without tuned upper ceilings. The ward keeps the values resolved when it forms.
Recovery starts when the ward forms and stays 12 seconds. A hit that spends the charge cannot also create another. Removing or changing the robe clears the charge without resetting recovery.
Normal attacks, fire and falls qualify. Damage that bypasses magical protection, including void and operator kill damage, does not.
Protected hits still cause robe wear once, even if all health damage is prevented. Forming a ward adds no separate durability charge.
items.example: With +25% Time, the ward lasts 5 seconds. With +25% Force and +25% Amplify, it prevents up to 3.125 HP on one hit. The first hit remains unchanged.
items.recipe: 4 matching Wool + 2 Callous Thread + Iron Ingot + Pufferfish

items.name: Cinderweave Robes
behavior: Prevent 25% of incoming fire-tagged damage, capped at 2 HP (one heart) per event, before ordinary armor and other protections.

Fire multiplies the percentage up to complete prevention. Amplify multiplies the per-event HP protection budget without a tuned upper ceiling. Actual protection uses the smaller result and cannot exceed the incoming hit.
Read current wearer traits for each fire event. An expired boost stops helping on later events; maximum mana remains a fixed +25.

Burning and lava qualify through Minecraft’s fire damage tag. Ordinary physical hits and damage bypassing magical protection do not. Strong boosts may fully protect an eligible fire hit; the robe grants no ignition.
A fire hit prevented by the robe still wears it once, including burning damage that would normally bypass armor wear. Merely wearing the robe adds no durability drain.
items.example: On an 8 HP fire event: baseline protection is 2 HP. +25% Fire alone still prevents 2 HP because of the cap; +25% Fire and +25% Amplify together prevent 2.5 HP.
items.recipe: 4 matching Wool + 2 Smoldering Thread + Blaze Powder + Magma Cream

items.name: Wayfarer Boots
items.control: Sprint, then jump from the ground (proposed)
behavior: A sprint-jump triggers 3 seconds of 20% faster movement when the ability is ready and affordable.
The next landing during those 3 seconds can prevent up to 2 hearts of fall damage once.
Normal jumps stay ordinary. Repeated jumps cannot refresh the burst or its landing protection.
items.example: Sprint-jump to cross a gap. You get a short speed burst and protection on one landing if it happens before the burst expires.
items.recipe: 4 Leather + 2 Laced Thread + Feather + Rabbit’s Foot
decisions: Approve the burst, fall protection, cost and recipe.
Choose whether every ready sprint-jump should activate it, or whether it needs a more deliberate control.

items.name: Dawnsight Hood
behavior: After preparing, reveal up to 8 invisible living creatures within 12 blocks for 6 seconds.
Require a clear line of sight to each creature when the reveal starts. Only the wearer sees the outline; invisibility stays intact.
Moving, entering combat or removing the hood cancels preparation without spending mana.
items.example: Pause and prepare to spot an invisible creature in an open room. The hood does not locate creatures hidden behind a wall.
items.recipe: 4 matching Wool + 2 Consecrated Thread + Glow Ink Sac + Glowstone Dust
decisions: Approve the reveal, range, duration, cost and recipe.
Choose the activation control; ordinary stationary crouching would also trigger the current proposal.
Choose whether the hood adds 10 maximum mana.

items.name: Patchwork Robes
items.control: Small four-pocket inventory (exact opening control undecided)
behavior: Four personal patches each store one object. The initial choices are Torch, Ladder, Oak Boat and a normal Compass.
Taking an object out empties its patch. Refill it with a real object; the robe does not generate replacement supplies.
Contents travel with this particular robe. There is no shared bag channel, full-stack storage or nested container storage.
items.example: Put a boat into a patch, then take that same boat out later. The patch stays empty until you put another object in.
items.recipe: 4 matching Wool + 2 Ensorcelled Thread + Ender Pearl + Chest
decisions: Approve four reusable storage patches, or revise the intended magic.
Choose the allowed objects, how to open the pockets, and whether access is available while worn.
Approve the recipe and shared robe values.

items.name: Spiderstep Boots
items.control: Hold jump against a wall; sneak to hold position
behavior: Climb a solid vertical wall at about 2 blocks per second. Holding still on the wall also spends mana.
Release the control, run out of mana, enter water, mount or remove the boots to detach. After detaching, ordinary falling applies.
No ceiling walking. Repeated short jumps cannot avoid paying for the climb.
items.example: A 10-block climb takes about 5 seconds and 10 mana, plus any time spent holding still.
items.recipe: 4 Leather + 2 Laced Thread + Spider Eye + Slimeball
decisions: Approve climbing, mana drain, controls and recipe.
Choose Red Laces, Web Cuffs, Spider Clasp or Climbing Wraps artwork.
